title: Search-Eval Verified Findings
description: Independent re-check of the worst-scoring terms before any of them becomes a finding. A term scores badly for one of two reasons - search really failed, or the CAPTURE failed - and the bottom of the ranking is disproportionately the latter. Target's board once showed 'dyson v8 -> Clorox cleaning wipes, grade 0.60'; the capture had grabbed a Recommended-for-you carousel, and the live site returns Dyson. Re-grading the same capture would have ratified the artifact, so verification MUST run through a different path than the one that produced the finding.

original_path.description: How the finding was originally captured.

verification_path.description: Must differ from original_path. Same-path re-capture confirms the artifact rather than testing it.

rule.description: How rows were chosen, e.g. 'bottom 20 by mean_grade' or 'every zero-result on a stocked term'. Recorded so the report can state coverage of the verification rather than implying all findings were checked.

verdict.description: confirmed - the failure is real and may ship as a finding. refuted - the original was a capture artifact and must NOT ship as a search finding. inconclusive - could not be re-checked; must not ship either.

reclassified_as.description: Why a refuted row scored badly. Refuted rows are not discarded: a run with several capture_artifact reclassifications is telling you the capture method is degrading, which is its own finding.

evidence.description: Replayable proof. A live URL a human can open, not a screenshot.

capture_quality_flag.description: Set when the refuted share is high enough that the capture method itself is suspect and the whole run should be re-examined before reporting.
